chapter_title: Concerning the Dragon with Fourteen Heads; what it is and [...]
chapter_note: Chapter 100 explicitly cites the Persian Magian tradition ('the laws of the Magi') as the source of the fourteen-headed dragon teaching. The core substrate is concentrated in paragraphs 4-6, which systematically map: 14 dragon heads → 7 upper sense organs + 7 lower body parts; 5 dens → tongue, lungs, heart, spleen, blood. The key identification (dragon = 'the thought of the body') appears in paragraph 7 embedded in exhortation. The teaching is framed by editorial dialogue (P1-2) and closed by a beatitude (P9). Despite the chapter's modest length, the body-correspondence substrate is remarkably clean and well-preserved. The explicit Persian provenance is significant — the teaching is presented as a spiritual reinterpretation of a Magian cosmological image, suggesting the substrate preserves an older Persian body-cosmos correspondence tradition.

paragraphs.core_text: there is a dragon with fourteen heads, and it is gathered in and [ ... ] den with five refuges.
paragraphs.removed_material: Dialogue frame opening '[Once again], one of his disciples asked the apostle [ ... ] is distributed [ ... ] the laws of the Magi. They say that'; honorific petition 'Now, I beseech you, my master, that you may instruct me about this lesson'; hermeneutical question 'What really is a corporeal dragon with fourteen heads? Or is it another spiritual lesson?' — all dialogue frame/editorial.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The disciple's question references 'the laws of the Magi' — explicitly sourcing the teaching to the Persian Magian tradition. The substantive cosmological content (14 heads, 5 refuges) defines the teaching structure and belongs to the oldest layer. The meta-question about corporeal vs. spiritual is pedagogical framing.

Entirely Mani's hermeneutical framing — 'Then the apostle says to him:' is dialogue attribution; the content positions Mani vis-à-vis the Magi ('the Magi did not understand'). The claim 'this is a spiritual lesson' is meta-commentary about the nature of correspondence, not a mapping itself. The substrate PRACTICES correspondence; this paragraph EXPLAINS that it is spiritual. That explanatory stance is editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this is how this earth [ ... ] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal dragon [ ... ] the dragon is this doctrine [ ... ] of the flesh [ ... ] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the dragon are these.
paragraphs.removed_material: 'I will instruct you' — first-person pedagogical dialogue frame voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose but contains core identifications: the earth/body is accounted as a dragon; the dragon = doctrine/thought of the flesh. Also introduces the enumeration of 14 heads. The lacunae make precise extraction difficult but the teaching structure is visible.

paragraphs.core_text: The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [ ... ] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure body-correspondence mapping: 7 sense organs on the head = 7 upper heads of the dragon. Systematic, impersonal, process-oriented. Note 'the different tastes that occur in every form' — taste-correspondence vocabulary characteristic of the substrate. Both sides of the mapping stay within the body-cosmos system.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the seven heads of the dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [ ... ] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [ ... ]; the two [ ... ] ruler [ ... ] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the dragon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the 14-head enumeration: 7 upper + 7 lower = 14 heads of the dragon. The seam flag on 'These are the' is a false positive — this is a teaching identification statement within the correspondence system, not an editorial bridge. Both sides remain within the body-dragon mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by] its fourteen heads.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps 5 dens → 5 internal organs with classic enumeration structure ('the first is... the second is...'). 'About which they have spoken' likely references the teaching tradition generically, not specifically the Magi as editorial target. The dragon's warfare through the 14 heads describes its cosmic-somatic function. Both sides stay within the body-correspondence system. Note the enumeration integrity: first through fifth preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: the dragon, which is the thought of the body
paragraphs.removed_material: Exhortation framing 'Whoever will recognise them with... and struggles with it and is victorious and kills it in them'; institutional titles '[ ... he is called] the holy righteous one, elect, good person'; eschatological promise 'He receives the victory without suffering on the day of his coming forth.' These are application/exhortation layers wrapping the core identification.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The key identification that completes the teaching structure: dragon = thought of the body. This is embedded in an exhortatory sentence about recognizing, struggling, and overcoming. The institutional vocabulary ('elect, good person') and eschatological reward ('the day of his coming forth') mark the application layer. The dragon-slaying motif may be ancient (Persian tradition), but the specific institutional and eschatological language is Manichaean editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: the dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [ ... / its des]ire all the time.
paragraphs.removed_material: 'So, behold, I have taught you of' — dialogue frame closure formula, first-person pedagogical voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulates the teaching structure (14 heads, 5 dens) and adds new process information: the dragon acts through the dens by desire. 'It does through them its desire all the time' describes how the dragon functions within the body-cosmos system — both sides stay within the system. The dialogue frame closure 'I have taught you' is stripped.

Classic devotional closure: dialogue frame ('Then that disciple says to him'), satisfaction formula ('My heart has been persuaded, my master'), beatitude ('Blessed is every one who will slay and kill it'), eschatological promise ('He will live for ever'). The beatitude formula 'Blessed is every one who' is a diagnostic marker of the exhortation layer. The dragon-slaying concept may be ancient but the devotional wrapper is editorial.
